messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Tidewave — recovery note and accountable action timeline

Hi Ayesha,

Thanks again for your patience this morning. Short summary upfront: between 07:42–08:10 UTC we saw elevated 5xxs and latency for requests routed to your region. The immediate cause was an unexpected KV-cache invalidation during a rolling configuration push; that triggered cache misses and retry storms which overwhelmed a small subset of serving pods.

What we did immediately:
- Rolled back the configuration change at 07:55 UTC (mitigated majority of errors)
- Increased pod capacity and disabled the problematic autoscale policy (07:58 UTC)
- Enabled cache warmup on the affected shard to reduce cold misses (08:05 UTC)

What's attached: a concise RCA summary (PDF) and an action timeline (CSV).

Next steps and owners (draft):
- short-term guardrail to block config keys that invalidate shared KV: Marissa Cole — target Nov 18
- autoscale policy audit and safety thresholds: Hannah Schmitt — target Nov 17
- durable cache design investigation and spec: Jonas Weber — target Nov 24

Please review the attached timeline and let us know if you prefer a recorded walkthrough or a short call to go through the technical details. We'll publish a public incident note to the status page after we confirm these dates with you.

Apologies again for the impact. We're treating this as a priority and will keep you updated with any material changes.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tidewave_rca_summary.pdf (PDF); action_timeline.csv (CSV)

Hi Ayesha — quick follow-up with the minute-level timeline and confirmations below. I've pasted the timeline and added an explicit data safety note. See also attached CSV with the timeline and a short runbook link.

Minute-level timeline (UTC):
- 07:42 — First spike: elevated 5xx rate observed on ~3% of requests routed to your model shard.
- 07:46 — Alerting triggered (error budget threshold). Autoscaler began scaling but was throttled by existing policy.
- 07:50 — Rolling configuration push started (this contained a KV key rotation; it triggered cache invalidation).
- 07:53 — Cache misses increased sharply; retries amplified traffic to a small subset of pods.
- 07:55 — Rollback of config push initiated by on-call; error rates begin to fall.
- 07:58 — Scaled pods increased and autoscale policy adjusted to allow emergency burst capacity.
- 08:05 — Cache warmup completed on affected shard; 5xxs returned to baseline by ~08:10.

Data safety: no persisted customer data was modified or lost. The failure was in the in-memory KV cache layer and request retries — we have confirmed there were no write-path errors and audit logs show no customer-data mutation during the window.

Scope and rollout ETA for durable cache design:
- Scope: introduce a per-deployment cache namespace and a staged invalidation API to avoid global invalidations during config changes; add pre-warm hooks for new code paths.
- Investigation phase (design + prototype): Nov 11–24 (owner: Jonas Weber)
- Internal review and safety testing: Nov 25–Dec 8 (owners: Jonas + Hannah)
- Canary rollout (small % of traffic): Dec 9–Dec 16
- Full rollout (if canary clean): target Jan 6, 2027

Action owners and commitments (confirmed):
- Marissa Cole — deploy configuration push guardrail (block invalidations) — target Nov 18 — PR/branch: github.com/redwood/ops/pull/482
- Hannah Schmitt — autoscale policy audit + emergency thresholds — target Nov 17 — JIRA SUP-7894
- Jonas Weber — durable cache design spec + prototype — target Nov 24

Links & attachments: the CSV timeline is attached; runbook: https://redwood-ops.example.com/runbooks/tidewave-kvcache; attached: tidewave_rca_summary.pdf, action_timeline.csv.

If you'd like a short 30-min follow-up to walk through the technical plan and the canary safety checks, we can schedule for next week — propose Nov 16 or 17.

Best,
Mina
